events.title: Rosa Parks Arrested in Montgomery
events.description: Rosa Parks, a Black seamstress and NAACP activist, refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in Montgomery, Alabama, and was arrested for violating the city's segregation laws.
events.significance: Her arrest sparked the 381-day Montgomery Bus Boycott, led by Martin Luther King Jr., which became a pivotal catalyst of the American civil rights movement and led to a Supreme Court ruling that bus segregation was unconstitutional.

events.title: Antarctic Treaty Signed
events.description: Twelve nations, including the United States, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and Japan, signed the Antarctic Treaty in Washington, D.C., setting aside Antarctica for peaceful and scientific purposes.
events.significance: The treaty prohibited military activity and nuclear testing on the continent and became a landmark model of international cooperation, entering into force in 1961.

events.title: Ford Introduces the Moving Assembly Line
events.description: Henry Ford's Highland Park plant in Michigan began using the first moving assembly line for mass production of automobiles, dramatically cutting the time needed to build a Model T.
events.significance: The innovation revolutionized manufacturing worldwide, made cars affordable to the middle class, and shaped modern industrial production.

events.title: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes Proclaimed
events.description: Following the collapse of Austria-Hungary at the end of World War I, the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes was proclaimed in Belgrade under Prince Regent Alexander Karađorđević.
events.significance: The new state, renamed Yugoslavia in 1929, reshaped the political map of the Balkans and its legacy influenced the region's history through the 20th century, including its breakup in the 1990s.

events.title: Channel Tunnel Workers Meet Under the English Channel
events.description: British and French construction workers broke through the final barrier of the service tunnel beneath the English Channel and shook hands, connecting the two countries underground for the first time.
events.significance: The breakthrough was a major milestone for the Channel Tunnel, which opened in 1994 and created a fixed rail link between the United Kingdom and continental Europe.
